steers.title: Trade cluster: HBAR + BTC
steers.detail: Both opened within 1 minutes. Correlation risk.

deep_analysis:
Bear structure, and the book is on the right side of it: 2 open trades, both SHORT, both under 1 hour, both regime-aligned (btc_4h SHORT_BIAS, btc_15m SHORT_BIAS, BTC below EMA300 for 1,302 consecutive 1m bars / 21.7h). The 24h ledger agrees with the positioning — LONG n=6 = -0.29 USDT at 16.7% WR vs SHORT n=2 = +0.07 at 50% WR.

BTC SHORT (16353): entry 81,139 while BTC sits under EMA300 81,566 — shorting from inside the trend filter's own bear zone, with SL 81,760 placed 0.24% ABOVE the EMA300 and TP 80,300 (planned R:R ~1.35). That is textbook invalidation placement: the stop is not a price level, it is the condition that proves the thesis wrong (a sustained EMA300 reclaim). Would I open it fresh today: yes. The honest risk is timing, not direction — BTC is mid-bounce (wyckoff ACCUMULATION, ewave W4, acceleration POSITIVE, 1m/5m linreg positive) so this squeeze can tag 81,760 before the W5 leg down. Losing that trade would still not make us wrong about the trend.

HBAR SHORT (16352): entry 0.079349 after a pump, meta_rsi 67.6 at signal time. Signal family volume-buildup- is the best current performer (9 trades, 77.8% WR, +0.35 USDT). Since entry HBAR's 5m has gone NEUTRAL with -0.92% over 16 candles — the pump is fading in our favor. SL 0.080928 (+2.0%) is ~6.3h of HBAR's 0.32%/h ATR, TP 0.077762 (-2.0%), R:R 1.0 — passes the gate but is the weakest part of the trade: we are risking a full 2% to make 2% on a mid-confidence setup. Would I open it fresh: yes, with caution — the RSI 67.6 entry sits above the 65 ceiling band (7d SHORT 65+ = -0.11, n=11), and the only defensible reason is the explicit bear-structure exemption (overbought pump in a bear = short), which btc_4h SHORT_BIAS satisfies.

Cluster is correlation, not over-exposure: HBAR and BTC opened within 60 seconds, but 2/6 slots, 100% one side, and that side matches the regime. The real concentration risk is that both trades share a single trigger — a BTC reclaim and hold of EMA300 ~81,566 (only 0.33% above current price, 0.24% below the BTC stop) takes out both at once, with HBAR's beta amplifying the second leg. If that reclaim holds, exit both manually rather than paying two correlated stops.

Enforced checks this cycle: regime alignment PASS (both short, both frames short-bias); +2% breakeven N/A (nothing up); +5% trail N/A (nothing up); 8h staleness N/A (both 0.5h old); directional exposure 2/6 = 100% short in a bear = correctly loaded, 4 slots free.

No AI-trader pick written this cycle, and that is deliberate: AI_TRADER_ENABLED = False (CEO 2026-10-19), and ai_trader_signal.run() returns before reading any state file — any pick written now is a no-op. The 16:47 FIL SHORT pick has also aged past the 45-minute TTL, and FIL has since flipped to NEUTRAL on the 5m scan (its own stated invalidation), so it was stale on both counts.

Sideways finds while verifying data sources: coin_tracker.db contains a single ancient 'TEST' row — the Coin Tracker dashboard's data source is dead (severity: warning, fix: restart its generator timer); watchdog pipeline_status.running = false is a false negative — the pipeline log shows clean cycles through 17:50 UTC.
regime_context:
Structure: btc_4h SHORT_BIAS, btc_15m SHORT_BIAS, continuum BELOW EMA300 for 1,302 consecutive 1m bars (~21.7h) at price 81,300 vs EMA300 81,566, trend_quality STRONG_DOWN, linreg LEAN_BEAR on 15m/1h.

Tape right now: a corrective bounce inside that downtrend — zscore recovered to -0.65 NEUTRAL (from STRONG_NEG earlier today), acceleration POSITIVE, 1m/5m linreg positive, wyckoff ACCUMULATION, ewave W4, market_phase CALM, volume_ratio LOW (0.14). In plain terms: the trend is down, the market is basing at the lows and grinding up toward the trend filter.

Volatility: LOW everywhere — 1h ATR: BTC 0.103%/h, HBAR 0.32%/h, FIL 0.23%/h. Low ATR is why both stops look "far" in percent terms: BTC's 0.77% stop ≈ 7.4h of ATR, HBAR's 2.0% stop ≈ 6.3h of ATR. Both are appropriately sized for this tape; neither is tight enough to be scalped by noise, and neither is loose enough to be a lottery ticket.

5m scanner aggregate: SHORT_BIAS 19 / LONG_BIAS 7 / neutral 97 — weak but correctly sided.

What it means for positions: shorts remain valid for as long as BTC stays under EMA300 81,566. A sustained reclaim flips the near-term read, invalidates BOTH open shorts, and is the only condition this cycle that should move us to exit. Longs stay blocked by the BTC ema300 gate until that reclaim holds — which is fine, because 24h LONG = 16.7% WR is exactly what that gate is protecting us from. If BTC instead loses the base and rolls over (W5), both shorts are on the right side of the next leg with stops already placed above the reclaim zone.
pattern_alerts:
PATTERN 1 — LONG-side bleed continues, and the winning side is obvious (VERIFIED, PostgreSQL, meta_rsi):
Last 20 closes (10-21 13:19 → 10-22 09:01): LONG n=18 = -0.62 USDT @ 38.9% WR; SHORT n=2 = +0.07 @ 50% WR. Narrower 24h window: LONG n=6 = -0.29 @ 16.7% WR (avg meta_rsi 48.9), SHORT n=2 = +0.07 @ 50%. Losers with meta_rsi: POL -0.22 (53.6, hard_max_loss), STX -0.11 (57.6, hard_max_loss), SYRUP -0.23 (44.8, stale_exit), INJ -0.08 (55.3, hard_max_loss), NEO -0.05 (52.6, atr_sl), BTC -0.04 (55.7, atr_sl), GRASS -0.08 (71.6, atr_sl), SOL -0.02 (32.7, atr_sl).
WINNING SIDE: short the same coins, or flat. POL, STX, NEO, INJ, SYRUP all kept falling after our long; BTC was under EMA300 through the entire hold so the winning side was shorting the bounce; SOL's oversold long (32.7) bought a knife that never bounced.
WHY WEREN'T WE ON IT: entries were mid-band meta_rsi 50-58 LONGs during a 21.7h BTC downtrend. The LONG_RSI_SWEET_SPOT (55-60) did not rescue them — RSI sweet spot only works WITH the trend, not against it.
Caveat (n checked both ways): 7 of the 18 LONGs did win (+0.36 gross) via profit-monster-trail — longs still pay when the entry runs immediately. So the leak is entry habitat, not longs as a class. Do not disable longs; do not take them under EMA300.

PATTERN 2 — Our SHORT pick guidance aims at the worst cell (VERIFIED, 7d, meta_rsi bands, direction=SHORT):
<45: n=7 = -0.21 (28.6% WR) | 45-55: n=13 = -0.46 (23.1% WR) | 55-65: n=6 = +0.28 (33.3% WR) | 65+: n=11 = -0.11 (36.4% WR).
WINNING SIDE: shorts that enter on an already-extended move (55-65) pay; mid-band shorts (45-55) fade nothing and get ground down. This matches independent constant-file evidence (PUMP_CHAIN 50-55 = 0% WR -$0.46; "RSI 55-65 SHORT = best, 71.4% WR") — two separate datasets agree on where the dead cell is.
WHY WEREN'T WE ON IT: the standing pick instruction says "SHORT at RSI 45-55, center of the allowed band" — that optimizes for gate-passing, not for the profitable cell. Flagged for the brain auditor (changing band constants is out of watchdog scope). Sample sizes are small (6-13 per cell): trust the direction (it agrees with the constants), not the magnitudes.

PATTERN 3 — Exit quality confirms the entry problem, not an exit problem (VERIFIED, 24h, n=8, total -0.22):
atr_sl_hit n=4 = -0.15, hard_max_loss n=1 = -0.22, stale_exit, atr_sl; the only wins were manual_tp_hit +0.11 and profit-monster-trail +0.04. 5 of 8 exits were stops. Entries never got traction — nothing to do with stop placement or trail logic (the trail machinery is the same one producing the +0.36 gross long winners).

NOT A PATTERN (checked and rejected): HBAR's meta_rsi 67.6 entry looks like a SHORT_RSI_CEILING (65) violation but is not — 65-75 carries an explicit bear-structure exemption and btc_4h is SHORT_BIAS, which is precisely the "overbought pump in bear = short" case the exemption exists for. Also rejected: "the bounce means shorts are wrong" — zscore NEUTRAL and 1m/5m linreg up inside a 21.7h below-EMA300 run is a W4 correction, not a regime flip.
